CYBERPUNK.Name: Name
CYBERPUNK.MartialArtBonusesHint: Per-action bonuses for this style. Used when the skill is selected as the Martial Art for an attack.
CYBERPUNK.Head: Head
CYBERPUNK.BlockParryText: Stop attacks with an object. Swords won't take damage, but must make a save to avoid breaking. You get -3 to your actions while blocking or parrying.
CYBERPUNK.DodgeText: -2 to attackers' hit rolls. You get -3 to your actions while dodging.
CYBERPUNK.DisarmText: Succeed? Opponent's weapon no longer in their hands.
CYBERPUNK.HoldText: Succeed? Opponent immobilized until escape made.
CYBERPUNK.EscapeText: Succeed? Their limbs are a prison that cannot hold you. You're free of opponent's Hold.
CYBERPUNK.SweepTripText: Succeed? Opponent knocked to ground, they get -2 to their next attack, and you get +2 to your next.
CYBERPUNK.GrappleText: Succeed? Great, now you can try to Hold, Choke or Throw your opponent.
CYBERPUNK.DodgeHint: Defensive: incoming melee attacks take -2 to hit this turn. You're at -3 to your own actions while dodging.
CYBERPUNK.BlockParryHint: Defensive: block or parry an incoming melee attack outright — no damage if you win the contest. Blades must save or break. -3 to your actions while blocking.
CYBERPUNK.StrikeHint: Punch attack — 1D3 + STR damage bonus + martial-art bonus. Contested vs the target's defense.
CYBERPUNK.KickHint: Kick attack — 1D6 + STR damage bonus + martial-art bonus. Hits harder than a strike. Contested.
CYBERPUNK.DisarmHint: Knock the target's weapon out of their hands on a successful contested roll.
CYBERPUNK.SweepTripHint: Knock the target prone: -2 to their next attack, +2 to yours. They must spend an action to stand.
CYBERPUNK.GrappleHint: Grab the target. While grappled you can Hold, Choke, or Throw them as a free action on later turns.
CYBERPUNK.HoldHint: Immobilize a grabbed target until they break free with Escape.
CYBERPUNK.ChokeHint: Strangle a held target: 1D6 damage per turn, and they must pass a Stun Save each turn or fall unconscious.
CYBERPUNK.ThrowHint: Throw the target down: 1D6 + STR damage and knocked prone (they must spend an action to stand).
CYBERPUNK.EscapeHint: Break free from an opponent's Hold or Grapple on a successful contested roll.
CYBERPUNK.PunchHint: Basic punch — 1D3 + STR damage bonus + martial-art bonus. Contested melee strike.
CYBERPUNK.RamHint: FNFF2: charging body-slam — drive into the target with your momentum.
CYBERPUNK.JumpKickHint: FNFF2: leaping kick — higher damage than a standard kick.
CYBERPUNK.CastHint: FNFF2: a throwing maneuver — hurl the opponent using their own momentum.
CYBERPUNK.AllOutParryHint: FNFF2: commit your whole turn to parrying for a strong defensive bonus — you can't attack.
CYBERPUNK.AllOutDodgeHint: FNFF2: commit your whole turn to dodging for a strong defensive bonus — you can't attack.
CYBERPUNK.AmmoTrackingHint: When on, weapons can't fire on an empty magazine — reload to draw from linked ammo. Turn off for Free Fire (ammo ignored, infinite reloads).
CYBERPUNK.SuppressiveDesc: Each creature inside or crossing the fire-zone rolls Athletics + REF + 1d10 vs DC ({save}).
CYBERPUNK.SuppressiveHitsDesc: On failure the target suffers 1D6 hits; each hit deals {dmg} damage to a random location.
CYBERPUNK.ReputationHint: Your social standing (CP2020 p.54). GM-set; can be negative for cowardice/infamy. Feeds the Facedown and Recognition rolls.
CYBERPUNK.FacedownHint: Roll 1d10 + COOL + Reputation. Target one foe's token first to make it a contested Facedown.
CYBERPUNK.FacedownSoloHint: Target one foe's token to make this a contested Facedown.
CYBERPUNK.FacedownPenalty: {loser} backs down — or is at −3 vs {winner} until they win a Facedown against them. (GM enforces.)
CYBERPUNK.FacedownTie: Tie — neither side backs down; no penalty.
CYBERPUNK.RecognitionHint: Roll 1d10 vs your Reputation: at or under = they recognize you; over = they haven't heard of you.
CYBERPUNK.RecognizedNo: Not recognized — rolled {roll} > Rep {rep}. They haven't heard of {name}.
CYBERPUNK.UnderThresholdMessage: Roll under the thresholds to succeed
CYBERPUNK.ItemDeleteConfirmText: Are you sure you want to delete {itemName}?
CYBERPUNK.DragItemsPrompt: Drag items here to add (for now)
CYBERPUNK.InitiativeTrackerWarning: At the moment, rolling initiative from the sheet doesn't add to the encounter's combat tracker.
CYBERPUNK.KeyTechniqueWarning: Key technique bonuses for martial arts aren't implemented yet

SETTINGS.FumbleTableEnabledHint: If enabled, whenever a skill check rolls a natural 1, the result is also determined using the fumble table.
SETTINGS.AutomationNoticeHide: Hide the Setup / What's New notice
SETTINGS.AutomationNoticeHideHint: When checked, the Cyberpunk 2020 setup & what's-new dialog stops appearing on load for the GM. Uncheck to see it again. (The notice's own 'Don't show this again' checkbox sets this too.)
SETTINGS.PlayersCanBuyAmmoHint: When off, only the GM can buy ammo; players are told they must purchase it at a shop and should ask the GM. Keeps ammo from appearing out of thin air.
SETTINGS.AmmoLockerEnabledHint: Optional, off by default. When on, any miscellaneous item can be turned into an 'Ammo Locker' (an in-inventory button that opens the ammo purchasing dialog). Leave off to buy ammo from the shop catalog's Ammo section instead.
SETTINGS.AmmoBlackhandsBoxes: Use Blackhand's Guide ammo box sizes
SETTINGS.AmmoBlackhandsBoxesHint: Optional. Switches firearm ammunition to Blackhand's Guide's uniform box-of-100 pricing instead of the Core rulebook's per-class box sizes. Default off (Core).
SETTINGS.AmmoBlackhandsBrassHint: Optional. Brass-cased loads cost x3 the base price (Blackhand's Guide) instead of x2 (Core rulebook). Default off (Core).
SETTINGS.ShoppingEnabledHint: Master toggle for the Shopping feature. When on, a 'Shop' button appears on character sheets and shops/purchases become available. Off by default (opt-in).
SETTINGS.PlayersCanShopHint: When off, only the GM can buy; players are directed to ask the GM. Keeps gear from appearing out of thin air.
SETTINGS.ShopBuySourceHint: What players can buy from when buying directly: the full catalog (all compendia), or only shops the GM has published.
SETTINGS.ShopAllowHomebrewHint: Off by default. When on, community / non-canon / cross-system items become available in the shop, where the GM can enable individual sources for players. Core and official R.Talsorian books are unaffected by this.
SETTINGS.ShopShowSource: Show item sources in the shop
SETTINGS.ShopShowSourceHint: Show a small badge on each shop item naming the book/source it comes from. Per-user — turn it off if you prefer cleaner rows.
SETTINGS.IpSystemHint: Off by default (free skill editing). Simple = one IP pool per character. RAW = the full per-skill Improvement Points tracker (GM-attributed awards, banked-per-skill, self-service level-ups).
SETTINGS.IpAwardModelHint: Manual = the GM types IP per skill use (RAW). Auto baseline = the GM ticks success on a queued roll and a fixed IP is granted automatically (the GM can still add bonus IP).
SETTINGS.IpAutoBaselineAmountHint: IP granted per GM-marked success when the award model is Auto baseline.
SETTINGS.IpThrottleHint: Optional secondary cap on farming one skill. Off = GM polices manually (default). Hard cap = one award per skill per Apply cycle. Diminishing = each further award on the same skill this cycle is halved.
SETTINGS.IpSkillLockModeHint: Who controls the skill-lock that prevents hand-editing skill levels/IP (rolling and confirm-button level-ups always work). Owner = the player. GM = the GM only. Mutual = a player soft-lock plus a GM hard-lock the player can't override.
SETTINGS.IpShowPendingHint: Show the GM-only “pending IP” pip on skill rows (pending IP is hidden from players until applied). Per-user.

CYBERPUNK.CatalogHiddenDivider: ⌄ Hidden from players (enable the source to sell these)
CYBERPUNK.CatalogSourcesHint: Tick a book to let players buy its items. You always see everything; disabled books show dimmed. This sets catalog-wide visibility — stock each shop separately.
CYBERPUNK.CatalogBooksEyeHint: Click a book's eye to show or hide its items from players. The filters here only change your own view.
CYBERPUNK.CatalogBookVisibleHint: Eye on = players can see & buy this book's items in the catalog. Eye off = GM-only. (This is catalog-wide visibility; stock custom shops to sell per-shop.)
CYBERPUNK.CatalogHomebrewOff: Enable “Allow homebrew content” in System Settings to use these.
CYBERPUNK.ShopFullSearchHint: Let players search & buy the whole (allowed) catalog here, with your curated items featured. Off = players see only the items you've added.
CYBERPUNK.ShopOnlyHint: Show only the items already added to this shop.
CYBERPUNK.ShopPreviewHint: Open the storefront the way players see it.
CYBERPUNK.ShopShowToPlayersHint: Open the shop to players and post a chat link they can click to browse and buy.
CYBERPUNK.ShopAlreadyStocked: That item is already in the shop.
CYBERPUNK.ShopBuildFooter: Search the catalog and ＋Add items to stock this shop. Set a per-item price (blank = catalog), Unlimited or a finite quantity, and tick Style-priced for clothing. Show to Players when ready.
CYBERPUNK.ShopManageHint: Switch back to the shop builder (GM).

SETTINGS.AutoFumbleOnlyJam: Automatic weapons: jam only on fumble
SETTINGS.AutoFumbleOnlyJamHint: Works only if the Fumble Table is enabled. If enabled, automatic weapons ignore the fumble table and only check for a jam using weapon reliability.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.Title: Reflex (Combat)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. You just screw up.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.6: 6. Weapon discharges or strikes something harmless.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.7: 7. Weapon jams, or knocks you to the ground for 1 round.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexCombat.9_10: 9–10. You manage to wound a member of your own party.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexAthletics.Title: Reflex (Athletics)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexAthletics.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. You just mess up and make an idiot of yourself.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexAthletics.5_7: 5–7. You fail miserably. Take 1 point in minor damage (sprain, fall, stumble), plus make a Save vs. Stun.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReflexAthletics.8_10: 8–10. You fail abysmally. If a physical action, take 1D6 in damage from falling or strained muscles. Also make a roll vs Stun at -1.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.Title: Control Loss Table
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.1_2: 1–2. Skid or slew; no other result.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.3_4.Ground: 3–4. Major skid; slide 1D10x10 feet sideways in direction of travel.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.3_4.Aircraf: 3–4. Aircraft stalls, losing 1D10x50 feet of altitude.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.5_6.Ground: 5–6. Roll ground vehicle after sliding 1D10x10 feet sideways in direction of travel; take 5D6 damage.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ControlLoss.5_6.Aircraf: 5–6. Aircraft goes into spin, lose 1D10x100 feet of altitude.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Tech.Title: Tech (Repair or create)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Tech.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. You just can't get it together.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Tech.5_7: 5–7. You not only fail, you make it worse! You drop the tools you're working with, or you lose your grip and damage the thing you're working with even more. Raise the Difficulty by 5 points and try again.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Tech.8_10: 8–10. Wow. Did you ever blow it! You damaged the device or creation beyond repair. Buy a new one.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Emp.Title: EMP (Convince, Fast talk, Seduce)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Emp.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. They just won't buy it.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Emp.5_6: 5–6. So much for your people skills. You not only don't convince them; you leave them totally cold (-4 to your next EMP die roll) to any other suggestion you might have.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Emp.7_10: 7–10. Yow! You blew it royally. You not only didn't convince them, but now they're actually violently opposed to anything you want to do. Roll 1D10. On a 1–4, they actually attempt to do you physical harm.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.EmpExtra.1_4: they actually attempt to do you physical harm.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.EmpExtra.5_10: they are violently opposed and resist you.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Int.Title: INT (Figure out, Notice, catch a clue)
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Int.1_4: 1–4. No fumble. You just don't know how to do it. You don't know what's going on. You carry on, oblivious to higher concerns.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Int.5_7: 5–7. You don't know anything about what's going on and you haven't a clue about how to do anything about it. Make a Convince check at -2 to see if anyone else notices how dumb you are.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.Int.8_10: 8–10. Wow, are you oblivious. You not only don't know what's going on or anything about the subject, but everyone knows how ignorant you are.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.AutoWeaponOnlyJam: Automatic weapons: fumble table is ignored; only a Reliability jam check is made.
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.ReliabilityResult.NoJam: lucky you, it didn’t jam - just a misfire
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.DischargeApplied: Result: the weapon discharged (ammo is now 0).
CYBERPUNK.Fumble.DischargeNotApplied: Result: lucky you, it didn’t discharge - just a misfire
